nodes.name: Non-Markovian Quantum Brownian Motion (QBM) master equation
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \frac{d\rho}{dt} = & -\frac{i}{\hbar} [H_0,\rho(t)]-\Delta(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{x},\rho(t)]] + \nonumber \\ & + \Pi(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{p},\rho(t)]] - i\gamma(t)[\hat{x},\{\hat{p},\rho(t)\}]\;, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Time-local QBM master equation with time-dependent damping $\gamma(t)$ and diffusion coefficients $\Delta(t),\Pi(t)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Hu, Paz & Zhang 1992; Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003; Maniscalco et al. 2004

nodes.name: Ohmic-like spectral density
nodes.statement: the rather typical Ohmic-like spectral density $J(\omega)=\omega e^{-\omega/\omega_c}$, where $\omega_c$ is the cut-off frequency of the bath.
differentia: $\omega_c$ is the cut-off frequency of the bath

nodes.name: High-temperature regime
nodes.statement: In the high-temperature regime, namely the case in which the classical thermal energy is much larger than the typical one that characterizes the system evolution, one has $K_B T \gg \hbar \omega_c, \hbar \omega_0$, where $\omega_0$ is the characteristic frequency of the system.
nodes.statement_short: Classical thermal energy dominates the system and bath scales: $K_B T \gg \hbar\omega_c,\hbar\omega_0$.

nodes.name: Non-Markovianity parameter $x$
nodes.statement: At any fixed given temperature and dimensionless time $\tau=\omega_c t$, the {\em non-Markovianity} parameter $x$ that characterizes the scales of the system time evolution identifies with the ratio between the bath and the system frequencies $x=\omega_c/\omega_0$: for $x\ll 1$, the dynamics is non-Markovian, otherwise it falls in the Markovian regime~\cite{PhysRevA.70.032113, TorreAsym2017}.
nodes.statement_short: $x=\omega_c/\omega_0$ is the bath-to-system frequency ratio; $x\ll 1$ marks the non-Markovian regime.
nodes.genus: the ratio between the bath and the system frequencies
differentia: for $x\ll 1$, the dynamics is non-Markovian, otherwise it falls in the Markovian regime

nodes.name: Two-mode squeezed vacuum shared entangled resource
nodes.statement: The shared Gaussian entangled resource is taken in the class of two-mode squeezed vacuum states $\rho_{12}=S_{12}(\zeta)\ket{00}_{12}\prescript{}{12}{\bra{00}}S_{12}(\zeta)$, where $S_{12}(\zeta)=e^{\zeta a_1^\dag a_2^\dag-\zeta^* a_1 a_2}$ is the two-mode squeezing operator, with $\Re(\zeta)=\cosh(r)$, $\Im(\zeta)=e^{\imath\phi}\cosh(r)$, and $r$ and $\phi$ are, respectively, the amplitude and the phase of the squeezing.
nodes.statement_short: The resource is a two-mode squeezed vacuum $S_{12}(\zeta)\ket{00}$ with squeezing amplitude $r$ and phase $\phi$.
differentia: $S_{12}(\zeta)=e^{\zeta a_1^\dag a_2^\dag-\zeta^* a_1 a_2}$ is the two-mode squeezing operator

nodes.name: Channel transit time $\delta\tau$
nodes.statement: This transit time is defined as the difference $\delta t=t_f-t_0$ between the instant $t_0$ when the resource mode starts to evolve in the channel, and the instant $t_f$ when it reaches Bob. In order to characterize the state evolution in the QBM channel entirely in terms of dimensionless quantities, we introduce the dimensionless channel transit time $\delta\tau=\omega_c \delta t$.
differentia: between the instant $t_0$ when the resource mode starts to evolve in the channel, and the instant $t_f$ when it reaches Bob

nodes.name: Teleportation fidelity in the non-Markovian QBM channel
nodes.statement: In terms of the parameters that characterize the states and the channel, the teleportation fidelity reads (details are reported in the Appendix below~\cite{SuppMat}): \begin{align} &\mathcal{F}(r,\phi,\delta\tau,x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{ -4\bar{W}_{12}^2(\delta\tau,x)+\dfrac{1}{4} e^{-2\Gamma(\delta\tau,x)} \Lambda_{11} \Lambda_{22} }} \, , \end{align} where \begin{align} &\Lambda_{jj}\!=\!\cosh 2r +e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau,x)}\!\!\left(\!\!2\!+\!4\bar{W}_{jj}(\delta\tau,x)\!+2\dfrac{\mathcal{R}^2}{\mathcal{T}^2}\!+\!\cosh 2r\!\!\right) \nonumber\\ & + \qquad\quad 2e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau,x)/2}\cos\left(\phi-\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x}\right)\sinh 2r , \quad j=1,2 \, . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form teleportation fidelity $\mathcal{F}(r,\phi,\delta\tau,x)$, whose phase dependence enters through $\cos(\phi-\delta\tau/x)$.
assumptions: In terms of the parameters that characterize the states and the channel

$\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{R}=\sqrt{1-\mathcal{T}^2}$ are, respectively, the transmissivity and the reflectivity of the beam splitters that model the losses of the realistic Bell measurement performed by Alice and include the effects of the noise affecting Alice's shared resource mode

nodes.name: Transmissivity $\mathcal{T}$ and reflectivity $\mathcal{R}$ of the Bell-measurement beam splitters
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{R}=\sqrt{1-\mathcal{T}^2}$ are, respectively, the transmissivity and the reflectivity of the beam splitters that model the losses of the realistic Bell measurement performed by Alice and include the effects of the noise affecting Alice's shared resource mode.
nodes.genus: the beam splitters that model the losses of the realistic Bell measurement performed by Alice
differentia: include the effects of the noise affecting Alice's shared resource mode

nodes.name: Phase-optimized teleportation fidelity
nodes.statement: Consequently, we introduce the phase-optimized fidelity: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}_{\textrm{opt}}(r, \delta\tau, x)=\max_{\phi}\mathcal{F}(r,\phi, \delta\tau, x) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Maximize the teleportation fidelity over the squeezing phase $\phi$ at fixed $r$, $\delta\tau$ and $x$.

nodes.name: Optimal squeezing phase $\phi_{\textrm{opt}}(x,\delta\tau)$
nodes.statement: Due to the positivity of the master equation coefficients $\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau, x)$ and $\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau, x)$~\cite{PhysRevA.80.062324}, one finds that at fixed $x$ and $\delta\tau$ the maximum in Eq.~(\ref{OptFid}) is achieved by \begin{equation} \phi_{\textrm{opt}}(x,\delta\tau)=\pi+\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x} \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The fidelity-maximizing squeezing phase is $\pi$ shifted by the transit time, $\phi_{\textrm{opt}}=\pi+\delta\tau/x$.
assumptions: Due to the positivity of the master equation coefficients $\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau, x)$ and $\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau, x)$~\cite{PhysRevA.80.062324}
conclusions: the maximum in Eq.~(\ref{OptFid}) is achieved by \begin{equation} \phi_{\textrm{opt}}(x,\delta\tau)=\pi+\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x} \, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Markovian limit of the optimal squeezing phase
nodes.statement: In the Markovian limit $x\gg 1$ we recover the known result~\cite{PhysRevLett.95.150503} that the optimal phase of the squeezing that maximizes the teleportation fidelity is $\phi_{\textrm{opt}} = \pi$, independent of the channel transit time.
conclusions: the optimal phase of the squeezing that maximizes the teleportation fidelity is $\phi_{\textrm{opt}} = \pi$, independent of the channel transit time

nodes.name: Extra preparatory step: select $\phi_{\textrm{opt}}$ from the transit time
nodes.statement: Therefore a further step has to be included in the preparatory stage of the protocol: the optimal phase $\phi_{\textrm{opt}}$ of the shared squeezed resource has to be selected in the laboratory according to the value of the transit time $\delta \tau$ of Bob's mode in the non-Markovian channel. In turn, the channel transit time is fixed in the experimental setup by the propagation velocity of the shared resource mode along the non-Markovian channel and the length of the latter.
nodes.statement_short: The squeezing phase must be set in the laboratory according to the measured channel transit time.

nodes.name: Squeezing amplitude fixed at the current technological limit $r=2.0$
nodes.statement: The squeezing amplitude $r$ of the entangled resource is fixed at $r=2.0$, a value corresponding to the current technological limit~\cite{SchnabelPrivComm}.

nodes.name: Essentially unit fidelity at lower $x$ and higher transmissivity
nodes.statement: Further lowering of $x$ and/or increasing of $\mathcal{T}$ at fixed squeezing realizes an essentially unity fidelity for longer channel transit times at lower temperatures.
assumptions: Further lowering of $x$ and/or increasing of $\mathcal{T}$ at fixed squeezing
conclusions: realizes an essentially unity fidelity for longer channel transit times at lower temperatures

nodes.name: Logarithmic negativity $E_{\mathcal{N}}$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} E_{\mathcal{N}}(\delta\tau)=\max\{0,-\log\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)\} \, , \end{equation} where $\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)$ is the smallest symplectic eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of the state evolved in the channel~\cite{1751-8121-40-28-S01}.
differentia: $\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)$ is the smallest symplectic eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of the state evolved in the channel

nodes.name: Equivalence between entanglement and optimal fidelity of ideal CV teleportation
nodes.statement: In the ideal, noiseless CV teleportation protocol with shared Gaussian entangled resource the optimal teleportation fidelity, i.e. the one obtained maximizing over all local single-mode operations, is in one-to-one correspondence with the entanglement of the shared resource, as first proved in Ref.~\cite{PhysRevLett.95.150503}.
assumptions: In the ideal, noiseless CV teleportation protocol with shared Gaussian entangled resource
conclusions: the optimal teleportation fidelity, i.e. the one obtained maximizing over all local single-mode operations, is in one-to-one correspondence with the entanglement of the shared resource

nodes.name: Markovian noise degrades the shared entanglement
nodes.statement: In the presence of Markovian noise the shared entanglement is still the key requirement for a reliable teleportation, but is quickly degraded~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}.

nodes.name: Recovery of the entanglement-fidelity correspondence under non-Markovian noise
nodes.statement: We see that indeed, in the presence of a non-Markovian dynamics the one-to-one correspondence between the shared entanglement and the optimal fidelity of the ideal noiseless protocol is essentially recovered.
assumptions: in the presence of a non-Markovian dynamics
conclusions: the one-to-one correspondence between the shared entanglement and the optimal fidelity of the ideal noiseless protocol is essentially recovered

nodes.name: Punctual non-Markovianity measure $\mathcal{N}_p$ for the QBM channel
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \mathcal{N}_p \!=\! \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1-\dfrac{\Delta(\delta\tau,x)}{\sqrt{\Delta(\delta\tau,x)^2+\gamma(\delta\tau,x)^2+\Pi(\delta\tau,x)^2}}\right]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Closed form of $\mathcal{N}_p$ for the QBM channel in terms of the coefficients $\Delta$, $\gamma$ and $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Fidelity revival tracks the channel non-Markovianity with a time delay
nodes.statement: At later times the fidelity, after a decreasing stage due to the destructive effect of the system-environment interaction, increases, due to the memory effect of the non-Markovian channel, as shown by the behavior of the non-Markovianity measure. An increasing non-Markovianity of the channel corresponds to an increasing teleportation fidelity, with a time delay.
nodes.statement_short: After an initial decay the fidelity revives, following the growth of $\mathcal{N}_p$ with a lag.
conclusions: An increasing non-Markovianity of the channel corresponds to an increasing teleportation fidelity, with a time delay

nodes.name: Origin of the time shift: $\tau_E \ge \tau_S$
nodes.statement: The time shift is due to the fact that the correlation time scale of the environment $\tau_E$ is equal or greater than the relaxation time scale of the system $\tau_S$, corresponding to the rate of change of the state of the system due to the system-environment interaction, quantified by $x=\omega_c / \omega_0 = \tau_S / \tau_E$. The time delay in the transmission to the system of the effect of the interaction with the environment can be well understood in terms of generic collisional models of non-Markovian channels~\cite{PhysRevA.87.040103}.
nodes.statement_short: The lag reflects $x=\tau_S/\tau_E$: the bath correlation time exceeds the system relaxation time.

nodes.name: Time and temperature window for non-Markovian effects
nodes.statement: Non-Markovian effects usually occur when the time evolution satisfies the condition $t \lesssim \tau_E=1/\omega_c$~\cite{PhysRevA.70.032113}. This relation is further constrained in the hight-temperature regime (See the Appendix below~\cite{SuppMat} for details). Indeed, since we have set $k_B T/\hbar\omega_c=10^2$, the characteristic frequency of the bath depends on the temperature through the relation $\omega_c\simeq 10^9 s^{-1} K^{-1} T$. Consequently, for $T\simeq 10^2 K$, the non-Markovian effects are maximally enhanced in the early stage of the evolution.
nodes.statement_short: Non-Markovianity requires $t \lesssim 1/\omega_c$, which at $T\simeq10^2$ K confines it to the earliest evolution stage.

nodes.name: Generality across the family of spectral densities
nodes.statement: The results of the present investigation encompass a large spectrum of interaction models, since they hold essentially for the entire family of spectral densities $J(\omega)=\omega_c(\frac{\omega}{\omega_c})^se^{-\omega/\omega_c}$, which for $s=1$ include the Ohmic case~\cite{PhysRevA.79.052120}. We have also considered the sub-Ohmic ($s=\frac{1}{2}$) and supra-Ohmic ($s=3$) cases, obtaining qualitatively very similar results.
nodes.statement_short: The conclusions persist for the whole $J(\omega)=\omega_c(\omega/\omega_c)^s e^{-\omega/\omega_c}$ family, including sub- and supra-Ohmic cases.

nodes.name: Non-Markovianity-assisted optimization of the teleportation protocol
nodes.statement: In summary, we have shown how, by engineering an appropriate time evolution regime, i.e. by fixing the value of the non-Markovian parameter $x$, and adapting accordingly the shared entangled resource, the efficiency of the CV quantum teleportation protocol can be optimized in terms of the phase of the squeezing of the shared resource, yielding a significant improvement of the teleportation fidelity.
nodes.statement_short: Engineering the non-Markovian regime and adapting the squeezing phase significantly improves CV teleportation fidelity.
assumptions: by engineering an appropriate time evolution regime, i.e. by fixing the value of the non-Markovian parameter $x$, and adapting accordingly the shared entangled resource
conclusions: the efficiency of the CV quantum teleportation protocol can be optimized in terms of the phase of the squeezing of the shared resource, yielding a significant improvement of the teleportation fidelity

nodes.name: Generalization to non-Gaussian squeezed-Bell resources
nodes.statement: The present study can be readily generalized to more general cases in several directions, for instance by considering non-Gaussian entangled resources of the squeezed Bell type~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}.

nodes.name: General resource theory of quantum non-Markovianity
nodes.statement: The present study might be also considered as a step forward towards the construction of a general resource theory of quantum non-Markovianity for quantum information and quantum technology tasks, along the lines outlined in Ref~\cite{BrandaoPRL2015}.
nodes.statement_short: Building a general resource theory of quantum non-Markovianity remains open.

nodes.name: QBM model: oscillator in a harmonic bath with position-position coupling
nodes.statement: We consider the dynamics of a quantum mechanical oscillator with characteristic frequency $\omega_0$ in contact with a bath of harmonic oscillators via a position-position coupling and a factorized initial state.

nodes.name: Hu-Paz-Zhang master equation
nodes.statement: \begin{align} \frac{d\rho}{dt} = & -\frac{i}{\hbar} [H_0,\rho(t)]-\Delta(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{x},\rho(t)]]+ \Pi(t)[\hat{x},[\hat{p},\rho(t)]] \nonumber \\ & -i\gamma(t)[\hat{x},\{\hat{p},\rho(t)\}]\;, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Appendix restatement of the exact time-local QBM master equation for the oscillator-plus-bath model.

nodes.name: Damping coefficient $\gamma(t)$
nodes.statement: \gamma(t)&\!=\!\alpha^2\!\int_0^t \, ds\int_0^{+\infty} \, d\omega J (\omega) \sin (\text{$\omega $s}) \sin (\text{$\omega_{0} $s}),
nodes.origin_citation: Hu, Paz & Zhang 1992; Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003

nodes.name: Normal diffusion coefficient $\Delta(t)$
nodes.statement: \Delta(t)&\!=\!\alpha^2\!\int_0^t \,\!\! ds\int_0^{+\infty} \, \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\! d\omega J (\omega) (2N(\omega , T)+1) \cos (\text{$\omega $s}) \cos (\text{$\omega_{0} $s}),
nodes.origin_citation: Hu, Paz & Zhang 1992; Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003

nodes.name: Anomalous diffusion coefficient $\Pi(t)$
nodes.statement: \Pi(t)&\!=\!\alpha^2\!\int_0^t \,\!\! ds\int_0^{+\infty} \, \!\!\!\!\!\!\!\! d\omega J (\omega) (2N(\omega , T)+1) \cos (\text{$\omega $s}) \sin (\text{$\omega_{0} $s}),
nodes.origin_citation: Hu, Paz & Zhang 1992; Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003

nodes.name: Mean photon number $N(\omega,T)$
nodes.statement: $N(\omega , T)=[\exp(\hbar \omega/K_B T)-1]^{-1}$ is the mean photon number

nodes.name: High-temperature approximation of the bath occupation
nodes.statement: We work in the hight-temperature regime, namely the case in which the classical thermal energy scale is much larger than the typical ones that characterize the system evolution ($K_B T \gg \hbar \omega_c, \hbar \omega_0$). Indeed, investigating the improvement of the efficiency of the protocol in this regime is particularly interesting, due to the strongly destructive effect of the system-environment interaction at high temperatures. In this regime we can set $2N(\omega, T)+1\approx \frac{2K_B T}{\hbar \omega}$ and determine the explicit expressions of the master equation coefficients for various classes of spectral densities~\cite{PhysRevA.80.062324}.
nodes.statement_short: In the high-temperature limit set $2N(\omega,T)+1\approx 2K_BT/\hbar\omega$ to evaluate the master-equation coefficients.

nodes.name: Characteristic function and displacement operator
nodes.statement: When considering continuous variable systems it is useful to represent the state $\rho$ in terms of the characteristic function $\chi(\rho)[\Lambda]=\textrm{Tr}[\rho D(\Lambda)]$, where $D(\Lambda)=\exp[i S^\intercal \Omega\Lambda]$ is the displacement operator,

nodes.name: Symplectic matrix $\Omega$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \Omega=\left(\begin{array}{cc} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{array} \right) \end{equation} is the symplectic matrix, $S=(\hat{x},\hat{p})^\intercal$ is the vector of quadrature operators, and $\Lambda=(x,p)^\intercal$ is the vector of coordinates.

nodes.name: Solution of the QBM master equation in the characteristic function description
nodes.statement: In the characteristic function description the solution of the master equation Eq.~(\ref{HPZEq}) is~\cite{PhysRevA.67.042108, PhysRevA.70.032113}: \begin{equation} \chi(\Lambda, t)=\chi(e^{-\frac{\Gamma(t)}{2}}R^{-1}(t)\Lambda, 0)e^{-\Lambda^\intercal \bar{W}(t)\Lambda}, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The QBM channel damps and rotates the argument of the characteristic function and multiplies it by a Gaussian noise factor.
nodes.origin_citation: Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003; Maniscalco et al. 2004

nodes.name: Noise matrix $\bar{W}(t)$, diffusion matrix $M(s)$ and rotation $R(t)$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} &\bar{W}(t)\!=\![R^{-1}(t)]^\intercal\!\!\left[e^{-\Gamma(t)}\!\!\!\int_0^t \!\!ds e^{\Gamma(s)}R^\intercal(s) M(s) R(s)\right]\!\!R^{-1}(t), \\ & M(s)\!=\!\left(\begin{array}{cc} \Delta(s)& -\Pi(s)/2 \\ -\Pi(s)/2 & 0 \end{array} \right), \\ & \\ \nonumber & R(t)=\left(\begin{array}{cc} \cos(\omega_0 t)& \sin(\omega_0 t) \\ -\sin(\omega_0 t)& \cos(\omega_0 t) \end{array} \right) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Definitions of the accumulated noise matrix $\bar{W}(t)$, the diffusion matrix $M(s)$ and the free rotation $R(t)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003; Maniscalco et al. 2004

nodes.name: Accumulated damping $\Gamma(t)$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \Gamma(t)=2\int_0^t \gamma(s)ds \, . \end{equation}
nodes.origin_citation: Intravaia, Maniscalco & Messina 2003; Maniscalco et al. 2004

nodes.name: Total initial state $\rho_0$ of input plus resource
nodes.statement: Let us denote by $\rho_{\textrm{in}}=|\phi\rangle_{\textrm{in}}\;_{\textrm{in}}{\langle\phi|}$ and $\rho_{\textrm{res}}=|\psi\rangle_{12}\;_{12}{\langle\psi|}$ the projectors corresponding, respectively, to the single-mode input state and with the two-mode entangled resource. The total initial state $\rho_{0}=\rho_{\textrm{in}} \otimes \rho_{\textrm{res}}$
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
nodes.genus: the projectors corresponding, respectively, to the single-mode input state and with the two-mode entangled resource

nodes.name: Characteristic function of the total initial state
nodes.statement: \begin{align} &\chi_{0}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}};x_{1},p_{1};x_{2},p_{2})= \nonumber \\ &\;\; =\textrm{Tr}[\rho_{0} \; D_{\textrm{in}}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}})\, D_{1}(x_{1},p_{1})\, D_{2}(x_{2},p_{2})] \nonumber \\ &\;\;\;\;= \chi_{\textrm{in}}(x_{\textrm{in}},p_{\textrm{in}})\; \chi_{\textrm{res}}(x_{1},p_{1};x_{2},p_{2}) \,, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The initial global characteristic function factorizes into input and resource characteristic functions.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: CV quantum teleportation protocol through a non-Markovian QBM channel
nodes.statement: Referring to the schematic representation of Fig.(1) in the main text, the first step of the protocol consists in a non-ideal Bell measurement performed by Alice, that is, an homodyne measurements on the first quadrature of the mode $1$ and on the second quadrature of the mode $\textrm{in}$. After such non-ideal Bell measurement, the remaining mode $2$ is left in a mixed state (see Ref.~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333} for details). The result is then communicated by Alice to Bob through a classical channel whose gain factor is $g$~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}. The mode $2$ of the resource is sent to Bob through the QBM channel Eq.~(\ref{HPZEq}), the state evolution being described by Eq.~(\ref{chiEvol}). After receiving the mode 2, Bob finally performs on it a displacement operation.
nodes.statement_short: Alice performs a lossy Bell measurement, sends the outcome classically, mode 2 traverses the QBM channel, and Bob displaces it.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise
input: a classical channel whose gain factor is $g$

nodes.name: Non-ideal Bell measurement by Alice
nodes.statement: the first step of the protocol consists in a non-ideal Bell measurement performed by Alice, that is, an homodyne measurements on the first quadrature of the mode $1$ and on the second quadrature of the mode $\textrm{in}$.
nodes.statement_short: Alice homodynes mode 1 and the input mode to realize a lossy Bell measurement.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Classical communication of the measurement outcome
nodes.statement: After such non-ideal Bell measurement, the remaining mode $2$ is left in a mixed state (see Ref.~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333} for details). The result is then communicated by Alice to Bob through a classical channel whose gain factor is $g$~\cite{PhysRevA.81.012333}.
nodes.statement_short: Alice sends the outcome to Bob over a classical channel of gain $g$.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Propagation of mode 2 through the QBM channel
nodes.statement: The mode $2$ of the resource is sent to Bob through the QBM channel Eq.~(\ref{HPZEq}), the state evolution being described by Eq.~(\ref{chiEvol}).
nodes.statement_short: Bob's half of the resource decoheres while travelling through the non-Markovian QBM channel.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Bob's conditional displacement
nodes.statement: After receiving the mode 2, Bob finally performs on it a displacement operation.
nodes.statement_short: Bob applies the displacement that completes the teleportation.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Characteristic function of the output teleported state
nodes.statement: \begin{widetext} \begin{align} \chi_{\textrm{out}}(x_{2},p_{2},\delta\tau) & = \chi_{\textrm{in}}(g \mathcal{T} x_{2}, g \mathcal{T} p_{2})\times\nonumber \\ & \chi_{\textrm{res}}\left( g \mathcal{T} x_{2},-g \mathcal{T} p_{2};e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} \left[x_{2}\cos(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})-p_{2} \sin(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})\right],e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} \left[x_{2}\sin(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})+p_{2}\cos(\dfrac{\delta\tau}{x})\right]\right) \times \nonumber \\ & \exp\left[-\left(\bar{W}_{11}(\delta\tau)+\frac{g^{2} \mathcal{R}^{2}}{2}\right)x_{2}^{2}- \left(\bar{W}_{22}(\delta\tau)+\frac{g^{2} \mathcal{R}^{2}}{2}\right)p_{2}^{2}-2 \bar{W}_{12}(\delta\tau)x_{2}p_{2}\right] \, , \end{align} \end{widetext}
nodes.statement_short: Output characteristic function: input times damped-rotated resource times a Gaussian noise factor from losses and the channel.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Ideal-protocol limit of the output characteristic function
nodes.statement: The characteristic function for the ideal protocol is recovered in the limits $\mathcal{R} \rightarrow 0$ $(\mathcal{T} \rightarrow 1)$, $g \rightarrow 1$ and $\delta\tau \rightarrow 0$ $(\Gamma(\delta\tau) \rightarrow 0)$~\cite{PhysRevA.76.022301,PhysRevA.81.012333}.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Teleportation fidelity in the characteristic function description
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}(\delta\tau) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int dx_2 dp_2 \; \chi_{\textrm{in}}(x_2, p_2) \chi_{\textrm{out}}(-x_2, -p_2,\delta\tau) \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Fidelity as the phase-space overlap integral of the input and output characteristic functions.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Covariance matrices of the input state and of the shared resource
nodes.statement: \begin{align} & \sigma_{\textrm{in}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{1}_2 \, , \\ & \sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi)=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\begin{array}{cc} A(r) & C(r,\phi) \\ C(r,\phi) & A(r) \end{array} \right) \, , \end{align}
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Blocks $A(r)$ and $C(r,\phi)$ of the resource covariance matrix
nodes.statement: \begin{align} &A(r)=\cosh(2 r)\mathbb{1}_2 \, , \\ &C(r,\phi)=\sinh(2 r)\left( \begin{array}{cc} \cos (\phi ) & \sin (\phi ) \\ \sin (\phi ) & -\cos (\phi ) \\ \end{array} \right) \, . \end{align}
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Covariance matrix of the output teleported state
nodes.statement: \begin{widetext} \begin{equation} \sigma_{\textrm{out}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!\!=\!\!\left\lbrace \frac{1}{2} e^{-\Gamma(\delta\tau) }\!\! \left[e^{\Gamma(\delta\tau) } g^2 \left(\mathcal{T}^2 \cosh (2 r)\!+\!2 \mathcal{R}^2\!+\!\mathcal{T}^2\right)\!+\!2 e^{\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}} g \mathcal{T} \sinh (2 r) \cos\left(\phi\!-\!\frac{\tau}{x}\right)\!+\!\cosh (2 r)\right] \right\rbrace\mathbb{1}_2+2\bar{W}(\delta\tau) \, . \end{equation} \end{widetext}
nodes.statement_short: Output covariance matrix combining squeezing, beam-splitter losses, gain and the channel noise $\bar{W}(\delta\tau)$.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Derivation of the teleportation fidelity Eqs. (2)-(3)
nodes.statement: It is now straightforward to obtain the teleportation fidelity from Eq.~(\ref{SingmaOut}). Indeed, due to the Gaussian nature of the input and output states, Eq.~(\ref{Fidelitychi}) can be written as: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}(r,\phi,\delta \tau)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\det[\sigma_{\textrm{in}}+\sigma_{\textrm{out}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)]}}. \end{equation} Replacing Eq.~(\ref{SingmaOut}) in Eq.~(\ref{GaussFid}) we finally obtain Eq.~(2) and Eq.~(3) of the main text.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation: use the Gaussian fidelity $1/\sqrt{\det[\sigma_{\textrm{in}}+\sigma_{\textrm{out}}]}$ and substitute the output covariance matrix.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Reduce the overlap integral to a Gaussian determinant formula
nodes.statement: Indeed, due to the Gaussian nature of the input and output states, Eq.~(\ref{Fidelitychi}) can be written as: \begin{equation} \mathcal{F}(r,\phi,\delta \tau)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\det[\sigma_{\textrm{in}}+\sigma_{\textrm{out}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)]}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Invoke the Gaussian fidelity identity $\mathcal{F}=1/\sqrt{\det[\sigma_{\textrm{in}}+\sigma_{\textrm{out}}]}$.
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Substitute the output covariance matrix and conclude
nodes.statement: Replacing Eq.~(\ref{SingmaOut}) in Eq.~(\ref{GaussFid}) we finally obtain Eq.~(2) and Eq.~(3) of the main text.
nodes.statement_short: Substituting $\sigma_{\textrm{out}}$ yields the main-text fidelity Eqs. (2)-(3).
nodes.section: Continuous variable quantum teleportation under non-Markovian noise

nodes.name: Two-mode characteristic function evolution in the QBM channel
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \chi(X,t)=\chi\left[(\mathbb{1}_2\oplus R^{-1}(t))X,0\right]e^{-X^\intercal(0_2\oplus\bar{W})X} \, , \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Only mode 2 of the resource is damped, rotated and noise-broadened by the channel.

nodes.name: Evolved covariance matrix of the shared resource
nodes.statement: \begin{widetext} \begin{equation} \sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!\!=\!\!\left[\mathbb{1}_2\oplus e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}}R^{-1}(\delta\tau)\right]^\intercal\!\!\sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi)\left[\mathbb{1}_2\oplus e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}}R^{-1}(\delta\tau)\right]\!\!+\!\!2\left[0_2\oplus\bar{W}(\delta\tau)\right] \, , \end{equation} \end{widetext}
nodes.statement_short: Congruence action of the damped rotation on $\sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi)$ plus the channel noise on mode 2.

nodes.name: Block form of the evolved resource covariance matrix
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \sigma_{\textrm{res}}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)=\left(\begin{array}{cc} A(r) & C(r,\phi,\delta\tau) \\ C(r,\phi,\delta\tau) & D(r,\phi,\delta\tau) \end{array} \right) \, , \end{equation}

nodes.name: Blocks $C(r,\delta\tau)$ and $D(r,\delta\tau)$ of the evolved covariance matrix
nodes.statement: \begin{align} & C(r,\delta\tau)=e^{-\frac{\Gamma(\delta\tau)}{2}}C(r,\phi)R^{-1}(\delta\tau) \, ,\\ & \nonumber \\ & D(r,\delta\tau)=e^{-\Gamma(\delta\tau)}A(r)-2\bar{W}(\delta\tau) \, . \end{align}

nodes.name: Smallest symplectic eigenvalue $\tilde{\nu}_-$ of the partially transposed covariance matrix
nodes.statement: Its expression in terms of the submatrices composing the covariance matrix Eq.~(\ref{SigEvolt}) is given by~\cite{1751-8121-40-28-S01}: \begin{widetext} \begin{equation} \tilde{\nu}_-(r,\phi,\delta\tau)=\sqrt{\!{\dfrac{1}{2}}\tilde{\Delta}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)-\dfrac{1}{2}\!\sqrt{\tilde{\Delta}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)^2 -4\det[\sigma(r,\phi,\delta\tau)^2]}} \, , \end{equation} \end{widetext} with: \begin{equation} \tilde{\Delta}(r,\phi,\delta\tau)\!=\!\det[A(r)]+\det[D(r,\phi,\delta\tau)]\!-\!2\det[C(r,\phi,\delta\tau)] \, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde{\nu}_-$ expressed through $\tilde{\Delta}=\det A+\det D-2\det C$ and $\det\sigma$.
assumptions: where $\tilde{\nu}_-(\delta\tau)$ is the smallest symplectic eigenvalue of the covariance matrix

nodes.name: Gaussian channel $(X,Y)$ representation
nodes.statement: The Gaussian nature of the QBM channel allows to characterize it in terms of two $2 \times 2 $ matrices $(X, Y)$, that act on the covariance matrix $\sigma$ of the input state as follows: \begin{displaymath} \sigma(t) = X(t)\sigma(0)X(t)^\intercal+Y(t) \, . \end{displaymath}
nodes.section: Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel

nodes.name: Complete positivity (CP) condition for a Gaussian channel
nodes.statement: For a Gaussian channel, the condition of Complete positivity (CP) is then expressed as: \begin{equation} Y(t)-\dfrac{\imath}{2}\Omega+\frac{\imath}{2}X(t)\Omega X(t)^\intercal \geq 0 \, , \end{equation} where $\Omega$ is the symplectic matrix defined in Eq.~(\ref{SympMat}).
nodes.section: Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel

nodes.name: Necessary and sufficient criterion for CP violation of the intermediate map
nodes.statement: In Ref.~\cite{PhysRevLett.115.070401} we have shown that in any interval $[t, t+\epsilon]$, violation of the CP condition occurs if and only if \begin{equation} Y(t+\epsilon, t)-\dfrac{\imath}{2}\Omega+\frac{\imath}{2}X(t+\epsilon, t)\Omega X(t+\epsilon, t)^\intercal < 0 \, , \end{equation} where the matrices $(X(t+\epsilon, t), Y(t+\epsilon, t))$ are given by the following relations: \begin{align} & X(t+\epsilon, t)=X^{-1}(t+\epsilon, 0)X(t,0) \, , \nonumber \\ & Y(t+\epsilon, t)=Y(t+\epsilon, 0)-X(t+\epsilon, t)Y(t,0)X^\intercal(t+\epsilon, t) \, . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The intermediate map on $[t,t+\epsilon]$ violates complete positivity iff a specific $2\times2$ matrix becomes negative.
nodes.section: Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel
conclusions: violation of the CP condition occurs if and only if \begin{equation} Y(t+\epsilon, t)-\dfrac{\imath}{2}\Omega+\frac{\imath}{2}X(t+\epsilon, t)\Omega X(t+\epsilon, t)^\intercal < 0 \, , \end{equation}

nodes.name: Punctual measure of non-Markovianity $\mathcal{N}_p(t)$
nodes.statement: A natural measure of punctual non-Markovianity, namely the non-Markovianity at any given time $t$, can then be defined in terms of the negative part of the spectrum of the matrix appearing in the l.h.s. of Ineq.~(\ref{CPINtMapViol}) as follows~\cite{PhysRevLett.115.070401,TorreAsym2017}: \begin{equation} \mathcal{N}_p(t)=\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow 0^+}\dfrac{\sum_{i=1}^2\left(\vert\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)\vert-\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)\right)}{\sum_{i=1}^2\vert\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)\vert} \, , \end{equation} where $\lambda_i(t+\epsilon, t)$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix on the r.h.s. of Ineq.~(\ref{CPINtMapViol}).
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{N}_p(t)$ is the normalized negative part of the spectrum of the CP-violation matrix as $\epsilon\to0^+$.
nodes.section: Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel
nodes.genus: A natural measure of punctual non-Markovianity
differentia: defined in terms of the negative part of the spectrum of the matrix appearing in the l.h.s. of Ineq.~(\ref{CPINtMapViol})

nodes.name: Explicit evaluation of $\mathcal{N}_p$ for the QBM channel
nodes.statement: The expression of the measure of non-Markovianity, Eq.~(\ref{NMarkMeas}) above, has been computed explicitly in Ref.~\cite{TorreAsym2017} for the QBM channel in terms of the channel coefficients Eqs.~(\ref{gamma})--(\ref{pi}) as functions of the dimensionless channel transit time $\delta \tau$ and is reported in Eq.~(6) of the main text.
nodes.section: Non-Markovianity measure of the QBM channel
